memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'Your servant guaranteed the boy's safety to my father. I said, "If I do not bring him back to you, I will bear the blame before you, my father, all my life!"'" — Gen 44:32 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Judah made a promise, and he intends to keep it. He put himself on the line as a guarantee for his brother's safe return, accepting lifelong blame if he failed.

A guarantee is a serious thing. It means one person's word standing behind another person's outcome. If the outcome fails, the guarantor pays.

Scripture uses exactly this idea about Jesus. He is called the guarantee — the surety — of a better covenant (Heb 7:22). He does not merely hope we make it home. He stands personally behind our arrival. He has put Himself on the line for our safe return to the Father.

The difference is that Judah could only promise to bear blame. Jesus actually bore it. Every failure that would have disqualified us, He carried to the cross and settled there. Our arrival home does not rest on our reliability. It rests on His guarantee, and He has never once defaulted.

If you have been worrying about whether you will make it — whether your faith is strong enough, your obedience consistent enough — hear this: your Guarantor is Jesus Christ. He is able to keep you from falling and to present you before God's glory without fault (Jude 24).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you find your assurance in your own performance or in Christ's guarantee?
2. Is there a promise you have made that you need to honour?
3. What would change today if you truly believed Jesus is standing behind your homecoming?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord Jesus, You are the guarantee of a better covenant, and my safety rests in You and not in myself. Thank You for bearing the blame I deserved. Keep me until the end. Amen.
